output.methodChoice: Kepner-Tregoe specification (IS/IS NOT on initial evidence), then ACH across the five hypotheses after reading the printer job log (X10) and ERP audit trail (X9), with a provenance check on the vendor and director accounts.
output.brief:
This is not an operator problem. The printer job records show that from 4 Oct 22:10, PackBridge sent a 36-month shelf life to the printers. No operator overrode anything, and the printed text matched what was sent. Before that date every Veltranol job used 24 months, including jobs run after the firmware change and jobs set up by agency operators. Two bad lots were also packed on Line 1 day shift by permanent staff. On 3 Oct, Regulatory Affairs entered a 36-month value for Veltranol that applies only from 1 Mar 2027. The 24-month value is still the one in effect, yet the live data used 36 months. The firmware and the agency operators are ruled out. The vendor's claim that future values cannot reach the line is wrong here, and I haven't found why. The camera only checks print against job data, so it passed every faulty carton.

What to do: don't warn or remove the agency operators. Keep the camera check on. Fix the Veltranol ERP record and hold every Veltranol lot packed since 4 Oct, including the two lots on Line 1 in the warehouse. Add a second-person check of printed expiry against the batch record at each setup. Check the other products edited under CC-309, especially the two with future start dates. Ask Corvane and IT why a future-dated value was used. I'm fairly confident; whether other products are affected is still unknown.
